As of April 2026, Pershing Square USA (PSUS) is also conducting a high-profile IPO for a new closed-end investment fund. Here is a breakdown of the top definitions: 1. Performance Share Units (Employee Compensation) Definition: A type of equity-based incentive granted to employees (often executives) that converts into company stock only if specific performance goals (e.g., earnings, total shareholder return) are met, usually over a 3-year period. Vesting: Subject to both performance criteria and continuous service. Taxation: Taxable as ordinary income upon the release/vesting date. Difference from RSUs: Restricted Stock Units (RSUs) usually only require time-based vesting, while PSUs are tied to performance metrics. 2. Power Supply Units (Computer Hardware) Definition: Components that convert high-voltage mains AC to low-voltage regulated DC power for computer internal components. Types: Modern PSUs are typically switched-mode, conforming to ATX specifications (latest: v3.1 as of mid-2025). Modular vs. Non-Modular: Modular units allow cable management to improve airflow, whereas non-modular units have soldered, fixed cables. 3. (ticker: PSUS), public on the NYSE, with a roadshow kicking off in April 2026. IPO Details: Shares are priced at $50 each. Structure: It is a "combined offering" where investors buying PSUS in the IPO may be eligible to receive shares in Pershing Square International (PSI). 4.
